articles.title: हिरासत में मौत मामला: मुआवजा न देने पर यूपी सरकार को हाईकोर्ट की फटकार - SabrangIndia
articles.search_term: ("हीट एक्शन प्लान" OR "गर्मी से राहत" OR चेतावनी OR "रेड अलर्ट" OR "ऑरेंज अलर्ट" OR "येलो अलर्ट" OR एडवाइजरी OR "राहत सामग्री" OR "राहत शिविर" OR मुआवजा) Uttar Pradesh
articles.full_text:
प्रीमा देवी बनाम उत्तर प्रदेश राज्य व अन्य मामले में 20 फरवरी 2026 को पारित फैसले में डिवीजन बेंच ने निर्देश दिया था कि मृतक के कानूनी उत्तराधिकारियों को तीन सप्ताह के भीतर 10 लाख रुपये का मुआवजा दिया जाए।
इलाहाबाद हाईकोर्ट की लखनऊ खंडपीठ ने हिरासत में मौत से जुड़े एक मामले में दिए गए अपने फैसले का पालन न किए जाने पर कड़ा रुख अपनाया है। अवमानना याचिका की सुनवाई करते हुए अदालत ने उत्तर प्रदेश सरकार के गृह विभाग के प्रमुख सचिव संजय प्रसाद को 31 जुलाई को व्यक्तिगत रूप से कोर्ट में उपस्थित होने का निर्देश दिया है।
जस्टिस सौरभ लवानिया की एकल पीठ ने टिप्पणी की कि डिवीजन बेंच के आदेश का अब तक पालन नहीं किया गया है। अदालत ने यह भी कहा कि संबंधित अधिकारी अवमानना अधिनियम की धारा 12 के तहत दंडात्मक कार्रवाई के दायरे में आते हैं।
द मूकनायक की रिपोर्ट के अनुसार, यह अवमानना याचिका (सिविल) संख्या 2110/2026, प्रीमा देवी बनाम उत्तर प्रदेश राज्य व अन्य मामले में 20 फरवरी 2026 को डिवीजन बेंच द्वारा पारित फैसले के कथित उल्लंघन के खिलाफ दायर की गई है। उस फैसले में अदालत ने पाया था कि मृतक की मौत राज्य अधिकारियों की हिरासत और नियंत्रण में हुई थी तथा रिकॉर्ड पर उपलब्ध सामग्री से संविधान के अनुच्छेद 21 के तहत मौलिक अधिकारों के उल्लंघन की पुष्टि होती है।
सुनवाई के दौरान कोर्ट ने डिवीजन बेंच के फैसले के महत्वपूर्ण अंशों का भी उल्लेख किया। अदालत ने कहा था, "कस्टोडियल टॉर्चर मानवीय गरिमा का सबसे क्रूर उल्लंघन है। यह न केवल पीड़ित के आत्मसम्मान को ठेस पहुंचाता है, बल्कि उसके अस्तित्व की जड़ों तक को झकझोर देता है। कस्टोडियल टॉर्चर मानवीय गरिमा पर एक सुनियोजित हमला है और जब भी मानवीय गरिमा पर आघात होता है, सभ्यता एक कदम पीछे चली जाती है।"
अदालत ने अपने फैसले में आगे कहा था, "राज्य अपनी हिरासत में रहने वाले व्यक्तियों के जीवन और स्वतंत्रता का संरक्षक होने के नाते उनकी सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित करने का सख्त और अहस्तांतरणीय दायित्व वहन करता है। इस दायित्व का निर्वहन करने में विफलता सार्वजनिक कानून के तहत राज्य की जवाबदेही को आकर्षित करती है।"
डिवीजन बेंच ने यह भी स्पष्ट किया था कि राज्य द्वारा दी गई व्याख्याएं न तो ठोस थीं और न ही पर्याप्त, जिससे यह अनुमान खारिज किया जा सके कि याचिकाकर्ता के बेटे की मौत जेल में हुई थी। अदालत ने सुप्रीम कोर्ट के निर्णयों का हवाला देते हुए कहा था कि आत्महत्या भी एक आंतरिक, जानबूझकर की गई चोट मानी जाएगी और यह अप्राकृतिक मृत्यु होगी, जिसकी जिम्मेदारी राज्य पर होगी।
मुआवजे के संबंध में डिवीजन बेंच ने निर्देश दिया था कि मृतक के कानूनी उत्तराधिकारियों को तीन सप्ताह के भीतर 10 लाख रुपये का मुआवजा दिया जाए। साथ ही, राज्य सरकार को निर्देश दिया गया था कि वह मोटर वाहन अधिनियम, 1988 के तहत उपलब्ध मल्टीप्लायर पद्धति की तर्ज पर उम्र, आय और आश्रितों जैसे प्रासंगिक मानकों को अपनाते हुए कस्टोडियल डेथ के मामलों में मुआवजा तय करने के लिए दिशानिर्देश तैयार करे।
न्यायमूर्ति सौरभ लवानिया ने कहा कि राज्य सरकार डिवीजन बेंच के फैसले का पूर्ण रूप से पालन करने में विफल रही है। अदालत ने कहा कि मृतक के कानूनी उत्तराधिकारियों को आदेशानुसार पूरे 10 लाख रुपये का मुआवजा अब तक नहीं दिया गया है। इसके अलावा, फैसले के पैरा 23 में दिए गए निर्देश के बावजूद कस्टोडियल डेथ के मामलों में मुआवजा तय करने संबंधी दिशानिर्देश भी राज्य सरकार ने अब तक तैयार नहीं किए हैं।
मामले की गंभीरता को देखते हुए अदालत ने कहा कि संबंधित अधिकारी अवमानना अधिनियम, 1971 की धारा 12 के तहत दंडात्मक कार्रवाई के पात्र हैं। कोर्ट ने निर्देश दिया कि उत्तर प्रदेश सरकार के गृह विभाग के प्रमुख सचिव संजय प्रसाद अगली सुनवाई पर व्यक्तिगत रूप से उपस्थित हों, जहां उनके खिलाफ आरोप तय करने की प्रक्रिया भी पूरी की जाएगी। अदालत ने स्पष्ट किया कि प्रमुख सचिव 31 जुलाई को न्यायालय के समक्ष अनिवार्य रूप से उपस्थित हों। मामले की अगली सुनवाई भी इसी दिन निर्धारित की गई है।

articles.title: Extremely Heavy Rainfall Alert: पूरे 7 दिनों तक मूसलाधार बारिश की चेतावनी, दिल्ली-महाराष्ट्र समेत इन सभी जगहों - CNBC TV18

articles.full_text:
Extremely Heavy Rainfall Alert: देश के कई हिस्सों में पूरे 7 दिनों तक भारी बारिश की चेतावनी जारी की गई है. महाराष्ट्र, पुणे, उत्तर प्रदेश, दिल्ली और गुजरात समेत और कई जगहों पर भारत के मौसम विभाग (IMD Alert) ने तेज हवाओं के साथ बारिश का अलर्ट जारी किया है.
29 जुलाई से 4 अगस्त के बीच देश के कई हिस्सों में बारिश होने की संभावना है. उत्तर भारत में हिमाचल प्रदेश, जम्मू कश्मीर, लद्दाख और उत्तराखंड में इस दौरान काफी व्यापक से व्यापक बारिश हो सकती है. हरियाणा, चंडीगढ़, दिल्ली (Delhi NCR Weather Update) और पंजाब में 30 जुलाई से 4 अगस्त तक बारिश की संभावना है. पश्चिमी उत्तर प्रदेश में 1 से 4 अगस्त और पूर्वी उत्तर प्रदेश में 2 से 4 अगस्त तक बारिश हो सकती है.
पूर्वी और पश्चिमी राजस्थान में भी 29 जुलाई से 4 अगस्त तक तेज हवाओं की संभावना है. मध्य प्रदेश, विदर्भ, छत्तीसगढ़, गुजरात, महाराष्ट्र, ओडिशा, झारखंड, बिहार, दक्षिण भारत के कई राज्यों और अन्य इलाकों में भी अलग-अलग दिनों में बिजली गरजने और तेज हवाओं की संभावना जताई गई है.

articles.title: Shrinking Forest Habitats Drive Escalating Tiger-Human Conflict in India - streamlinefeed.co.ke
articles.full_text:
The increasing frequency of tiger sightings in human-dominated landscapes across northern India is not an indicator of dangerous overpopulation, but rather a direct symptom of severe habitat fragmentation, according to leading wildlife experts analyzing the region's ecological stress.
Speaking from Dehradun, Uttarakhand, prominent wildlife photographer and conservation documentarian Arzoo Khurana highlighted the critical misconception driving local anxieties regarding big cat encounters. "First of all, I would like to share that the number of tigers is not decreasing; rather, the forest area is shrinking," Khurana stated on Wednesday. "Because of this, tigers are coming out into human-inhabited areas more frequently." This spatial crisis, driven by unchecked infrastructure expansion and agricultural encroachment, mirrors the acute human-wildlife conflict currently destabilizing conservation efforts around East Africa's premier national parks.
The Corridor Crisis in Uttarakhand
Uttarakhand, home to the globally renowned Jim Corbett National Park and the Rajaji Tiger Reserve, represents one of the world's most vital tiger landscapes. While stringent anti-poaching measures and dedicated conservation programs have successfully stabilized and marginally increased the apex predator's population, the geographical footprint available to these territorial animals has simultaneously contracted.
Tigers are highly solitary and demand vast territorial ranges to hunt and breed successfully. A single male tiger can require a territory ranging from 60 to 100 square kilometers. When critical wildlife corridors—the natural forested pathways connecting larger protected areas—are severed by new highways, expanding townships, or agricultural clearing, younger tigers are forced to migrate into peripheral human settlements to establish their own domains. This forced proximity inevitably results in livestock depredation, panic among local communities, and tragic retaliatory killings of the endangered cats.
Data: The Anatomy of Habitat Loss
The intersection of population recovery and habitat loss creates an unsustainable ecological mathematical equation.
- Territorial Requirements: Adult tigers require vast, exclusive hunting domains to survive.
- Corridor Degradation: Key transit routes between protected zones are increasingly bisected by linear infrastructure.
- Spillover Effect: Sub-adult tigers, pushed out by dominant older males, are the primary demographic entering human settlements.
- Conflict Escalation: Increased interactions lead to elevated livestock losses and retaliatory wildlife poisonings.
The Global Human-Wildlife Conflict Bridge
The spatial dynamics articulated by Khurana in Uttarakhand find exact parallels in the savanna ecosystems of Kenya and Tanzania. The Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) is currently grappling with identical challenges on the peripheries of the Tsavo East and Amboseli National Parks. In Kenya, expanding agricultural footprints and the subdivision of traditional Maasai group ranches have severely disrupted historic elephant and lion migration corridors.
The financial toll of this proximity is staggering. The Kenyan government regularly faces a backlog of hundreds of millions of shillings (millions of USD) in unpaid compensation claims for crop destruction, livestock predation, and human injury. Whether dealing with a tiger in Dehradun or a lion in Kajiado County, the fundamental policy failure remains the same: state governments prioritize isolated protected areas while neglecting the broader ecological connectivity required to sustain megafauna. Without legally protected buffer zones and strict zoning laws preventing industrial expansion into wildlife corridors, the friction between apex predators and rural economies will only intensify.
Looking Ahead: Rethinking Conservation Architecture
Addressing the root cause of this conflict requires a paradigm shift in how regional governments approach land-use planning. Conservationists are aggressively lobbying for the legal recognition and protection of wildlife corridors as critical national infrastructure, equivalent in importance to highways or power grids. This includes constructing dedicated wildlife underpasses across major transport arteries and providing substantial financial incentives to rural communities that agree to maintain forested buffers.
Ultimately, the survival of the species depends not just on counting the animals inside the parks, but on securing the landscapes outside them.
As habitats compress, the margin for error between successful conservation and ecological catastrophe vanishes entirely.

articles.title: NASA’s High-Resolution 3D Model Reveals Earth as an Asymmetrical Gravitational ‘Lumpy Mess’ - streamlinefeed.co.ke
articles.full_text:
From the freezing vacuum of deep space, the Earth appears as a pristine, geometrically perfect \"Blue Marble.\" However, a radically new, high-resolution visualization released by NASA strips away the optical illusion of perfection, revealing our planet as a bizarre, asymmetrical, and highly irregular mass of gravitational hills and valleys.
This striking geoid model, compiled from 15 years of exhaustive satellite telemetry, provides unprecedented insights into the Earth’s uneven mass distribution. Far from being a mere scientific curiosity, this lumpy, exaggerated rendering offers critical, real-time intelligence for climatologists tracking catastrophic global ice loss and hydrologists mapping the rapid depletion of subterranean groundwater reserves.
What Exactly Is a Geoid Model?
To comprehend NASA’s visualization, one must discard standard topographical maps based on physical terrain. A geoid is a complex mathematical model that illustrates exactly how the surface of a global, planet-wide ocean would settle if it were influenced exclusively by the Earth’s gravity and its rotational axis, completely devoid of external variables like tidal forces, atmospheric winds, or shifting ocean currents.
Because the Earth’s interior is a chaotic mix of varying densities—ranging from ultra-dense tectonic rock formations to sprawling subterranean magma chambers—the planet’s gravitational pull is not uniform. Regions containing dense, heavy material exert a slightly stronger gravitational force, pulling water toward them to create subtle \"hills.\" Conversely, areas with lower-density crust produce a weaker pull, resulting in vast gravitational \"valleys.\"
In reality, these fluctuations only amount to elevation differences of a few hundred feet across thousands of miles, completely imperceptible to the naked eye. To make the invisible forces visible, NASA exaggerated the geoid’s variations by a massive factor of 10,000. The resulting data shows that the highest point in Earth’s gravitational field peaks near Iceland at approximately 279 feet above the global average, while the deepest gravitational trough plunges 348 feet below average just south of the Indian subcontinent.
How Do Satellites Measure Gravity Over Time?
Achieving this level of sub-millimeter precision required a fleet of highly specialized orbital instruments. The model synthesizes over a billion individual measurements collected primarily by NASA’s Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE) satellites, its successor GRACE-FO, and the European Space Agency’s GOCE mission.
These twin satellites fly in tandem, separated by roughly 137 miles. As the lead satellite approaches a gravitational anomaly—such as a dense mountain range or a rapidly melting ice sheet—the slight increase in gravity pulls it forward, momentarily increasing the distance between the two crafts. Microwave ranging systems measure these microscopic shifts in distance, allowing supercomputers on the ground to map the Earth’s gravity field with breathtaking accuracy month after month.
What Does the Data Reveal About Global Ice and Groundwater Loss?
The GRACE dataset has become the ultimate indisputable ledger of global climate change, as changes in gravity directly correlate to the massive displacement of water and ice. NASA’s highly calibrated observations reveal terrifying metrics regarding polar instability.
The data confirms that the Antarctic ice sheet has been hemorrhaging approximately 135 gigatons of solid ice per year between 2002 and 2025. Concurrently, the Greenland ice sheet is collapsing at an even faster trajectory, shedding an average of 264 gigatons of ice annually. By measuring the precise gravitational weight of these shrinking landmasses, oceanographers can accurately calculate exact contributions to rising global sea levels.
Furthermore, the satellites are highly sensitive to acute shifts in shallow soil moisture and deep aquifer levels. Recent GRACE telemetry clearly maps the severe, long-term groundwater depletion accelerating across the agricultural belts of the western United States, as well as the intense drought conditions currently fueling massive summer wildfires across Spain and France.
How Can This Data Enhance Climate Resilience in East Africa?
The applications of this orbital technology extend far beyond the polar regions, offering a critical lifeline for equatorial nations battling severe climate volatility. In Kenya, vast tracts of Arid and Semi-Arid Lands (ASALs) face chronic drought cycles that devastate pastoralist communities and agricultural outputs.
Institutions such as the Nairobi-based Regional Centre for Mapping of Resources for Development (RCMRD) increasingly rely on advanced satellite data to monitor subterranean water tables. By utilizing gravitational anomaly data, geologists can accurately track the depletion and recharge rates of deep underground aquifers in regions like Turkana, long before wells run dry on the surface.
Gravity is no longer just an abstract physical constant holding us to the ground; it has evolved into a vital, dynamic diagnostic tool, providing humanity with a stark, unvarnished look at a rapidly shifting world.

articles.title: Raging Wildfires Force Evacuation of 10 Villages on Greek Island of Paros - streamlinefeed.co.ke
articles.full_text:
Ferocious northerly winds have transformed a brush fire near a rural landfill into a raging inferno on the Greek tourist island of Paros, forcing the emergency evacuation of 10 villages as flames bore down on coastal communities.
The blaze, which erupted on Tuesday afternoon in the Kampi area, highlights the escalating climate risks Mediterranean tourist destinations face during the peak summer season. Despite massive aerial and ground interventions, authorities struggled through Wednesday to contain multiple advancing fire fronts on the island's southern and southeastern flanks.
Midnight Evacuations and Panic
What began as a localized fire burning through waste and low vegetation quickly escalated as gale-force winds pushed the flames through dry grass, farmland, and rugged terrain. As night fell and firefighting aircraft were grounded due to visibility limits, the fire intensified, triggering a frantic, coordinated retreat.
Greece's Civil Protection Authority issued four successive emergency alerts via the national 112 warning system, instructing thousands of residents and vacationers to abandon their properties and hotels.
- First Wave: Residents of Agios Charalambos, Kampi, Bougados, Aneratza, and Kamari were ordered to evacuate toward the coastal safe zone of Aliki.
- Second Wave (1:30 a.m.): The fire breached the wider Agkairia region, prompting immediate evacuation orders for all inhabitants to head to Aliki beach.
- Third Wave (2:15 a.m.): As a secondary front advanced toward Trypiti and Faragas beach, authorities ordered the evacuation of Trypiti, Aspro Chorio, Glyfa, and Pyrgaki toward the eastern village of Drios.
Paros Mayor Konstantinos Bizas described the overnight battle as exceedingly difficult, noting that the fire had scorched large tracts of land along the road to the Monastery of Agioi Theodoroi. Extensive power cuts have also plunged much of southern Paros into darkness.
The Firefighting Offensive
By first light on Wednesday, the Hellenic Fire Service launched a massive counter-offensive. The operation involved 66 professional firefighters, four specialized forest commando teams, and 16 heavy fire engines operating on the ground.
To supplement local forces, reinforcements were transported by ferry from the neighboring islands of Naxos and Syros, with an additional 20 firefighters and eight engines dispatched from the mainland port of Rafina. Airborne operations resumed at dawn, with two Canadair water-bombing aircraft and five helicopters pounding the active fronts near Agkairia and Faragas.
Deputy Mayor for Civil Protection Charalambos Giourtzidis confirmed that while the fire had been partly contained near Trypiti, volatile wind patterns continued to carry embers over long distances, sparking unpredictable new flare-ups in the parched brush.
A Mediterranean Climate Warning
Greece endures destructive wildfires almost every summer, but prolonged droughts and climbing average temperatures have created ideal conditions for explosive fire behavior. Paros, the third-largest island in the Cyclades archipelago, attracts nearly one million tourists annually, making summer evacuations logistically complex and economically devastating.
In response to previous catastrophic fire seasons, the Greek government has completely overhauled its civil defense strategy. The nation currently deploys 18,000 professional and seasonal firefighters, supported by 85 state-owned aircraft. Furthermore, authorities have established over 100 drone surveillance bases in high-risk zones to detect thermal anomalies before they explode into uncontrollable infernos.
Global Tourism and Ecological Echoes
The chaotic scenes on Paros serve as a stark warning for tourism-dependent economies worldwide, bridging the Mediterranean crisis to destinations in East Africa and the Asia-Pacific.
For nations like Kenya, which heavily markets its coastal resorts in Diani and Malindi, the Greek emergency illustrates the direct threat extreme weather poses to hospitality revenue. An uncontained disaster can obliterate a region's international appeal overnight. Just as the Bank of Greece monitors the fiscal fallout from disrupted European holiday travel, the Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) continuously evaluates how global climate shocks might impact foreign exchange earnings from international arrivals.
The Greek strategy of integrating drone surveillance and aggressive early-warning SMS systems offers a scalable blueprint for developing nations facing their own climate-induced disasters, from forest fires in Mount Kenya National Park to sudden flash floods in the Rift Valley. Upgrading emergency response infrastructure is no longer an optional luxury, but a fundamental requirement for protecting both civilian lives and sovereign economic interests.
As ground crews on Paros continue to douse smoldering hotspots, local officials maintain a high-alert posture. With winds expected to persist, the battle to save the island's southern communities remains far from over. For now, the immediate priority is survival, but the long-term challenge of adapting to a warming world will define the future of global tourism.
